label: letter c input late in the original sequence (position >= 5)
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the letter c during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position 5 or later. Never fires on c at positions 0-4, on any other token, at the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase. At position >= 6 it fires on every c (precision 1.0 on dev); at position 5 it fires only weakly and on a minority of cases (these are the lowest-quartile activations, ~0.02-0.1 of max), which accounts for most false positives. Magnitude grows with position: the largest activations (~2.7-2.8) are c at position 8 just before <DEL> in L=9 sequences, mid-range ~1.0-1.7 at positions 6-7. Neighbouring tokens, first token, repeats and digit count have essentially no effect.

issues: Every claim I checked holds. The feature never fires outside the original phase: 0 activations at the delimiter step or in the copy phase on dev. It never fires on any token other than c, and never at t <= 4. The test split has 0 missed activations and mass recall 1.0.
All false positives (5337 on test) are c at t == 5. On dev, precision for c at t == 5 is about 0.51-0.52 whatever L is (6, 7, 8 or 9). Precision is 1.0 at t = 6, 7 and 8.

I looked for history variables that separate the t == 5 cases that fire from those that don't. Only weak effects showed up: a digit as the previous token raises precision to 0.71, but that covers only 1440 cases. in_first, seen(c), in_count, n_digits, first_tok and prev2_tok all leave precision at 0.48-0.61. So the t == 5 cutoff behaves like a magnitude ramp crossing the activation threshold, not a hidden systematic class. This matches the explanation's 'weak, lowest quartile' wording: the t >= 6 predicate covers quartile 1 at 0.0.

Magnitude does grow with position. Activation mass per active step rises from t=6 to t=7 to t=8, and t=8 (only in L=9 sequences, at the last token before <DEL>) holds the largest values, with max 2.816.

The label says position >= 5, which slightly overclaims for position 5, where only about half of the c inputs fire. The explanation states this correctly. The alternative t >= 6 predicate scores test F1 0.852 (precision 1.0, recall 0.742), lower than the 0.894 of the reported t >= 5 predicate.
